question: Can explicit physical line addressing preserve exact source bytes when source-to-relation/prose generation failed?
hypothesis: Line-addressed copying removes semantic interpretation requirements. Exact copying may succeed without supporting any claim of semantic understanding, source discovery, bilingual prose or complete notes. Failures further narrow basic serialization/attention boundary.
primary_metric: 9 exact full source line strings, including indentation; no newline terminator or number prefix. Missing/changed whitespace is failure under exact-byte criterion.
secondary_metric: Whitespace-stripped code equality descriptive only; never substitutes primary acceptance.
stop: First HTTP/timeout/length/invalid JSON/schema failure halts batch, no retries.
limits: Three development-exposed source families; operator supplies explicit addresses. Nine distinct target lines not independent document/language trials. No complete document requested and none can be accepted.
